# Cape Town Wind Factory

> A proposed FAI competition-grade vertical wind tunnel (Tunnel Tech TT65 PRO, 6.5 m diameter, 24 m high flight chamber) at the V&A Waterfront, Cape Town, South Africa. The first indoor skydiving facility of this scale in Africa. Total development cost R200 million; R100 million (50%) secured; R100 million sought from investment partners. Led by Ruben Knoetze, National and International Springbok Skydiving Champion with more than 50 years in the sport.

The project consists of three connected proposals that share one facility and one leadership:

1. Investment Proposal — the commercial facility. Audience: investors and funding partners. Ask: R100m, the remaining 50% of the R200m development cost.
2. The Cape Town School of Human Flight (SOHF) — inclusive indoor skydiving for people with disabilities (spinal cord injuries, paraplegia, amputations, cerebral palsy, autism, visual impairments) and a pathway into FAI-recognised Indoor Para Skydiving. Audience: disability-sector sponsors. Ask: sponsorship of flights, bursaries, adaptive equipment, instructor training and athlete development.
3. Community Transformation Through Human Flight — youth development, STEM education, social cohesion and skills pathways for historically disadvantaged communities. Audience: CSI and government social-development partners. Ask: sponsorship of youth, education and outreach programmes.

Key facts:
- Location: V&A Waterfront, Cape Town (specific venue within the precinct to be finalised).
- Facility: TT65 PRO by Tunnel Tech. 6.5 m chamber diameter, ~24 m height, two levels of 54 mm glass, 55 dB(A) noise emissions, FAI competition standard, supports 4-way and 8-way Formation Skydiving, Dynamic disciplines and Indoor Para Skydiving.
- Market: indoor skydiving exceeds €1 billion annually, 300+ facilities worldwide, 20 million+ flights. FAI adopted Indoor Para Skydiving in 2025 as its first para-sports discipline; World Cup debuted in France, April 2026; inaugural FAI World Championships March 2027.
- Timeline after site and funding close: engineering and design ~3 months; construction and fit-out 8–10 months; testing and commissioning ~2 months; soft launch ~1 month.
- Revenue streams: public flights and athlete training; international training camps and competition hosting; coaching, instruction and corporate events; hospitality, conferencing and retail; sponsorship, branding, media and broadcasting.
- Status: proposed development, in active discussion with investors. Figures are indicative pending due diligence. A Non-Circumvention and Non-Disclosure Agreement applies to the detailed proposals.
